tasks.title: Zombie repopulation — density becomes bodies

CLOSES PL-M2-05 / PL-M4-26, and gives PL-M4-02 / PL-M4-10 (inert type-only nodes) a body. node.walkers is written in exactly three places: seedWorld.ts:79 (init), combat.ts:269 (-1 on a kill) and events.ts:440 (the seedWalkers encounter effect, 4 uses in content). NOTHING in the director, the drift model, the hordes or the difficulty dials ever adds one back — the player monotonically strips a finite city and the map never refills. Consequently region.zombieDensity and region.threat, the two dials the whole escalation story runs on, are read only by the director, regionDrift and pacing telemetry: they never become a zombie, a wound, or a decision. Pin zombieDensity at 100 today and the only observable difference is one narration line. Fix: add a repopulate pass to the regions layer (pipeline stage 7). Per node per tick, spawn probability proportional to region.zombieDensity and biased toward the loudest and most-recently-searched nodes, bounded by a per-node ceiling AND a region-wide budget so it can never manufacture an impossible state (GDD XVI rule: the director biases, it never forces). Draw zombieTypes from a density-gated table so a high-density region seeds Riot/Bloated/Fresh rather than just more walkers. Also fix enemyForNode's type/population divorce — a node with zombieTypes ['zombie.riot'] and walkers 3 currently spawns THREE Riots (10h and ~92% bite risk each in melee), while the same node with walkers 0 is never offered a fight at all; store a per-node roster instead of walkers:number + zombieTypes:string[]. INTENTIONAL behaviour change, not byte-identical; heed the PL-M4-54 / byte-identity-loot-hazard lesson and watch that the new draws don't silently shift existing RNG streams — give repopulation its own named stream. The moment this lands, the director, the drift model, the noise chain and all four difficulty dials acquire teeth simultaneously; every other gameplay task in M4/M5 is cheaper and less important than this one. Shipped: sim/roster.ts (a per-BODY roster; walkers and zombieTypes are derived from it, so killing the riot leaves walkers behind it instead of two more riots) and sim/repopulate.ts (the regions-layer pass, banked hours per T74, its own repop:<regionId> stream per region, bounded by a per-node ceiling + a region capacity + hard exclusions on the player's node and their shelter, never culls, killable with world.flags['repopulate.disabled']). tasks.title: Horde collision — noise acquires a bill
tasks.note: Design review 2026-09-12 (docs/qa/DESIGN_REVIEW_2026_09.md) step 3. state.hordes had NO mechanical consumer: outside sim/hordes.ts it was read by coreActions.ts:437 (one narration line), telemetry/pacing.ts and the history log. A horde standing on the player's node spawned nothing, blocked nothing, wounded nothing - so FIRE_NOISE 75 vs MELEE_NOISE 15, the designed counterweight to the firearm, re-pathed a mass that could not matter when it arrived. DONE 2026-09-12 (docs/qa/QA_REVIEW_T76.md). Shipped: sim/overrun.ts (the collision - while a mass stands on you there is NO fight choice at all, only run or go to ground; the branch sits ABOVE combat in availableActions so a horde walking into a duel does not queue behind it, and both verbs end the fight and abandon any engaged encounter; escape roll is max(0.6, detectChance) so it costs something even at night in fog; on a hit, one wound per 16 bodies (1-3) from its OWN table where a bite is 1 row in 5 rather than the walker table's 1 in 2, because at 1-in-2 a two-wound overrun infects ~75% of the time and the horde stops being pressure and becomes an execution; the hold is NEVER omitted, so the branch can never hand back an empty choice list - the PL-M5-14 softlock class) and a rewritten sim/hordes.ts (seeding is content-driven: one mass per region whose AUTHORED zombieDensity clears 50, sized 8-40 from it, placed furthest by hop count from the start node; a body trade with every node ENTERED - shed onto contested ground under its nodeCeiling, absorb the last plain walker off ground over it, nothing on a quiet node or at the ceiling - bounded by T75's own nodeCeiling so the two systems agree what a district holds, conserving sum(rosterOf(node).length)+sum(horde.size) exactly; and a step-at-a-time walk INTERLEAVED across the hordes so one N-hour advance lands byte-identically where any chunking of those N hours lands). The overrun is DERIVED, not stored - nothing added to GameState at all, so save v10 holds with no rung. sim/hordes.ts#overrunsPlayer is the SINGLE definition of the collision, read by availableActions, evaluateEvents, recordHistory and the harness soundscape. Engine 675 -> 726, harness 262 -> 264. MEASURED before -> after: hordes at seed 1/24 -> 3/95; horde steps over 30 off-screen days 180 -> 540 (57 of 60 nodes touched); map bodies at day 30 132 -> 101 with the rest carried (mass 24 -> 120); quiet nodes 11/60 -> 10/60 (seed-dependent: also 12->11, 11->12, 8->10, so shadowing is roughly neutral); scripted never-fight runs spend 0/24/0/0/0 turns standing under a mass with NO CONSEQUENCE WHATSOEVER -> 0/8/0/4/6 turns for 2-18 wounds; tickHordes one-shot == chunked over 480h on the 60-node city, which the BASELINE is not (machine-shop vs loading-canal); overrun outcomes over 200 seeds: detected 61% (the floor exactly), 2.00 wounds per detection, bite wounds 23% of wounds. AVOIDABLE, measured not asserted: the one-hop world lead preceded 18 of 18 overruns, and a player who moves away when it fires takes 12 overruns over 304 turns where the same player ignoring it takes 18 over 261 (3.9 per hundred turns vs 6.9), surviving about a sixth longer - FR-CBT-08's 'routed or fled, never out-traded' earning its pass for the FIRST time, since through T75 it passed only because the horde had no teeth. CORRECTIONS this task's own note got wrong, measured not argued: (1) HORDE_HOURS_PER_STEP STAYS 4 - T74's accumulator already made a horde advance on an ordinary turn (180 steps over 30 days of 2h turns, not zero), and at 2 a horde's 2h/node would exactly match the player's own MOVE_COST so a fleeing player could never gain ground, the opposite of FR-CBT-08. (2) THREE hordes, not 4-6 - counterfactual on the finished build with the threshold at 1 so all six regions seed: overrun on 12-22 of 41-58 turns for 12-28 wounds, every seed dead day 4-5; at three, 0-8 of 40-60 turns for 2-18 wounds with two of five seeds never meeting a mass. Six does not make the horde deadlier so much as constant. Three also leaves Rivermouth - the START region - clean, so a mass is something you meet by pushing into the three richest districts. (3) It does NOT close PL-M2-05: that is slip/retreat ignoring route conditions, it belongs to T77, and T76's flight REUSES escapeTargets and inherits the hole. (4) 'a horde on a high-density node grows' is INVERTED - a horde grows by absorbing from a node OVER its ceiling, and higher density means a higher ceiling. (5) 'a horde that sits on a node adds walkers per tick' - the trade fires on node ENTRY, which is what carries the chunk-exactness. (6) spawn/split/merge were NOT built (hordes.length is invariant for a run). (7) FR-CBT-08 is satisfied for FLED and routed, not FUNNELED - there is no funnelling mechanic. (8) The fun-gate 'prints for twenty consecutive turns' symptom is a two-node-ITINERARY artefact: on the shipped city the old lead fires 0 times in 500 parked turns and no mass ever arrives either, so the real complaint was INVISIBILITY. COSTS DECLARED, not discovered: the claimed shelter is a HARD SANCTUARY from the whole system until T83 - no bodies shed there, no collision standing in it - because repopulate.ts reserves the base assault for T83, 'not this pass's to sneak in' (PL-M5-18); a horde cannot be DISPERSED, since a shed needs a body already standing there, so HORDE_MIN_SIZE never binds while HORDE_MAX_SIZE binds constantly (PL-M5-16); Horde.types is dead state and no spawn/split/merge exists (PL-M5-17); advanceWorld(200000h) goes 5ms -> 231ms, linear in hours (PL-M5-19); the overrun is scaled by NONE of difficulty.ts's five dials and leaves no pacing signal, parked rather than added dead per the T56/T74/PL-M5-11 lesson (PL-M5-20); and the M4 exit-gate manifest still has no horde/FR-CBT-08/FR-SIM-07 entry (PL-M5-21, T57's). Two declared chunking differences: the noise re-path is evaluated once per tick, and the mass traded reads region density once per span (positions stay exact, sizes do not - measured 23/29/37 one-shot vs 33/37/40 chunked over 240h). THREE AUDIT PASSES. Pass 1+2: conservation broken by withRoster's entry filtering and reachable from an authored zombieTypes typo; resolveOverrunAction had no precondition, so an unvalidated bare 'hold' wounded the player on 16 of 30 seeds with no horde on the map; three leaks of the hordes.disabled flag; a NaN reaching state.history and making the save lossy; two BLOCKER over-claims in prose ('seeds six, totalling 156' when it seeds three totalling 95, and 'can only ever reduce encounter shadowing' when the system effect is seed-dependent); roster laundering that re-emitted an authored special as a plain walker; and T75's shelter promise being broken SILENTLY. Pass 3 - the verification pass - earned its budget again: it caught that the worldLead 'fix' had made its own problem WORSE (widening to two hops fired on 23% of parked turns against the pre-fix build's 16%; reverted to one hop, 7 fires in 500 turns with a longest run of 2, and it lost no warning at all), that the shelter exclusion had not been carried to the Living History or the encounter guard (fixed by giving the rule ONE definition), that the delta credit could breach HORDE_MAX_SIZE (39 -> 42), and that two mutants survived all 722 tests - one of them under a test whose TITLE claimed to cover it. 18 mutations applied and reverted; all are now killed by a named test. tasks.title: Close the noise → arousal → detection chain
tasks.note: Design review 2026-09-12 (docs/qa/DESIGN_REVIEW_2026_09.md) step 4 — cheapest high-impact change in the review. CLOSES PL-M2-02 (couple the T25 state machine to combat/stealth). detectChance(noise, phase, weather) takes THREE inputs: p = clamp(0.25 + noise*0.005 - phaseConcealment/100 + weatherDelta/100, 0, 0.9). Everything else the fiction promises is excluded. NodeState.zombieState — the entire T25 arousal ladder (dormant/wandering/investigating/chasing/feeding, WANDER_AT 8 / INVESTIGATE_AT 20 / CHASE_AT 40, PLAYER_HERE_BONUS 40, SCENT_BONUS 15, STALKER_NIGHT_BONUS 30, SWIFT_BONUS 25, the screamer cascade) is consumed ONLY by three narration strings at coreActions.ts:445-450. CombatState.alerted is written at combat.ts:307 and :320 and read in no condition anywhere, so retreating from a fully alerted enemy is the same roll as slipping past one that never noticed you. woundBurden() is exported and imported by nobody. inventoryWeight never touches stealth, noise or movement cost — CARRY_CAPACITY 40 is a pure inventory cap, so a full pack of loot walks home exactly as quietly as an empty one. Fix, essentially one signature: pass zombieState and alerted into detectChance and add +0.10/+0.25/+0.40 for wandering/investigating/chasing, +0.20 when retreating from an alerted fight, woundBurden/10 (the SCENT_BONUS fiction already exists in zombies.ts — a bleeding player is trackable), and max(0, (inventoryWeight - PACK_HEAVY)/10). Two related holes worth taking in the same pass: escapeTargets (combat.ts:176) filters only on discovered and does NOT check isBlocked(routeWear(...)) or add extraCostOf(wear) the way move does (coreActions.ts:171-174), so standing at a walker node lets you slip across routes travel refuses — walkers are currently a fast-travel network; and SLIP_COST === MOVE_COST === 2 makes avoidance completely free at the margin. Also fix the PLAYER_HERE_BONUS 40 == CHASE_AT 40 collapse — any occupied node reads 'chasing' the instant you stand on it, at zero noise, in any weather. INTENTIONAL behaviour change, not byte-identical (stealth rolls move). Payoff: noise -> arousal -> detection becomes one closed causal chain instead of three disconnected systems, and it retroactively gives the Screamer, the Stalker, alerted, woundBurden and pack weight a purpose. || UPDATED 2026-09-12 (T76 done): T76 REUSES combat.ts#escapeTargets for the horde overrun's flight, so the isBlocked/routeWear hole this task owns is now load-bearing in TWO places, not one - fixing it here fixes the overrun's flight at the same time. T76 also did NOT close PL-M2-05 despite its own note claiming to: PL-M2-05 IS that route-wear hole and it belongs to this task. escapeTargets is now exported and documents the hole in place. || DONE 2026-09-12. docs/qa/QA_REVIEW_T77.md. Full CI: engine 759 (was 726 at T76) / harness 264 / content-loader 23 / schema 160 / a11y OK. Save v10 holds - nothing added to GameState, the read is DERIVED. Shipped: sim/detection.ts (new, the composed read: base + arousal + alerted + scent + pack, percentage points, clamped once at DETECT_MAX 0.9); actions/costs.ts (new leaf module so combat.ts can define SLIP_COST = MOVE_COST + 1 without an import cycle); PLAYER_HERE_BONUS 40 -> 25 (it EQUALLED CHASE_AT); scentDraw() makes the T25 scent bonus a gradient on woundBurden with SCENT_FULL_AT = a bite's severity; escapeTargets honours isBlocked/routeWear; escape labels carry move's road suffix; combatNarration names the loudest term (signpost, don't retune). MEASURED before -> after on the shipped city (runner COMMITTED at prototype/harness/measure/t77.ts, so the numbers are re-derivable): slips at a chasing node 168/168 (100%) -> 84%, and the first slip of all 40 runs is now at `investigating`, a state that was literally unreachable; hours an escape dodged vs the same move 36 -> 0; mean composed detection at an escape 0.254 -> 0.587; slip wound rate 29.9% -> 60.5%; retreat 44.8% -> 76.0%; mean end day 4.0 both ways (thirst still kills first). The read now ESCALATES across a run - 0.414 at slip 1, 0.669 by slip 10+ - which is the inverse of the review's 'being hurt makes the world safer'. CORRECTIONS TO THIS NOTE, all measured: (1) AROUSAL_DETECT is 5/15/30 not 10/25/40 - at the brief's numbers the mean roll was 0.716 with 15% pinned at the ceiling, i.e. the roll stopped varying, this task's own failure from the other side; (2) ALERTED_DETECT 15 not 20; (3) woundBurden/10 and (weight-PACK_HEAVY)/10 re-scaled to percentage points (as probability the first is +4.0 and the second +0.01); (4) the blocked-route filter must NOT be unconditional - PL-M2-05's own text says the hole was deliberate so a fight can never strand the player, and FR-CBT-05 is a Must, so a blocked road is refused only while another is passable and forcing the last crossing is charged the worst rate; (5) PL-M2-02 is only HALF closed - the state machine is coupled, no per-type combat behaviour was added and the Screamer gains nothing specific (PL-M5-26). AUDIT (3 passes) caught a BLOCKER I had written into a comment: the first draft justified an unconditional filter with 'no route on the shipped content ever blocks', which is false - tickWeather degrades RegionState.roads monotonically and never restores them, so a route blocks on day 9-10 under storm and 14-15 under snow, and because decay hits every region alike the player could be left with ['fight'] as their entire choice list. Also fixed: scentDraw was not total (a NaN wound switched the WHOLE arousal ladder off), clampPoints failed open on Infinity, T77 created a `feeding` discount under the player's feet, stealthTell was dead code, and 3 cited PL ids did not exist. 22 mutants, 20 killed by a named test; 3 survived the first round and every one was an audit fix made WITHOUT a test - the T75/T76 lesson, third time.

Three audit passes: engineering (six findings incl. a non-finite clock making every wound fresh forever, and all six wound-stamp sites unprotected by any test), honesty (nine over-claims incl. the low band 'reachable only in a pacified district' - false, day-1 only), verification (every fix re-mutated and killed by a named test, every quoted figure re-derived on both trees). Closes PL-M2-03, the upward-driver half of PL-M4-26, PL-M5-09's tide correction, PL-M5-24.] Design review 2026-09-12 (docs/qa/DESIGN_REVIEW_2026_09.md) step 7. CLOSES PL-M2-03 remainder and the upward-driver half of PL-M4-26; feeds T60. Four mechanisms currently push the threat curve DOWNWARD. (1) playerDistressed (director.ts) returns true if ANY wound has treated < 100, and wounds.ts never lowers a wound with the passage of time — so after your first fight you are permanently 'distressed', the director sits in relief essentially forever and pushes zombieDensity down by 1 every turn. The comeback rope is the only beat it ever plays, and the game gets easier the worse you are doing. (2) The regionDrift equilibrium (20 + trunc(threat*3/5) - trunc(survivorActivity*2/5), threatTarget = trunc(density/2) + trunc(fire/2), and fire is never written by anything) is a stable LOW fixed point that ignores the authored baseline entirely: simulated over 400 turns both shipped regions converge to ~threat 18 / density 28, so Downtown's authored 70/80 'richest and most dangerous ground in the city' has a half-life of about four in-game days. (3) pressureRead locks at 21-23, permanently below DIRECTOR_LOW_BAND 25, so directorBeat returns 'escalate' every tick forever — a bang-bang controller pinned at one output, which also means the T30 Definition of Done ('disabling the director changes pacing metrics') passes trivially. (4) There is no day-based ramp anywhere: day 40 is identical to day 2 except the map has fewer zombies on it. Fix: narrow the wound clause to a real burden threshold (woundBurden >= 60) or a wound opened within the last 6 hours; add a dayFloor term such as min(40, meta.day) to pressureRead so the low band stops being reachable by week two; cap relief beats per 24h; and anchor equilibriumDensity/threatTarget on the region's authored RegionDef.baseline so regional identity survives contact with the simulation. Depends on T75 (the dials must be able to become bodies first). Not byte-identical; this is the task that makes T60's pacing telemetry worth reading.

Small, ~10 lines, and it inverts the single most backwards fact in the world sim. DESIGN §5 and GDD IV both say leave a district to fester and it gets worse; the code does the opposite. tasks.title: Weapon profiles & the missing combat verbs
tasks.note: Design review 2026-09-12 (docs/qa/DESIGN_REVIEW_2026_09.md) step 5. FR-CBT-02 (Must/VS) + FR-CBT-04 (Must/VS) + FR-PLR-04 (Must/VS). Combat has a total dominant strategy and the reason is arithmetic: resolveFire (combat.ts:312) spends one ammo, deals a flat FIRE_DMG 3, ignores armor and NEVER CALLS enemyRetaliate — firing is mathematically incapable of hurting you. Against a walker, melee costs E[2.25h] with a 56% chance of a wound and a 30% chance of the bite that starts the infection clock; a bullet costs 1h at 0% and 0%. Against a Riot (5hp, armor 1) melee is E[10h], E[4.5 wounds] and a 92.5% chance of a bite, versus two rounds and two hours. And the designed counterweight, FIRE_NOISE 75, only bites once T76 ships. Meanwhile melee damage is drawInt(1,2) REGARDLESS of what you hold — an equipped weapon's only effect is wearWeaponOnStrike (durability -1), a broken weapon carries no combat penalty, and item.molotov has no combat action at all (PL-M4-30). So FR-PLR-04 is currently inverted: equipment defines maintenance cost, not capability. Fix: (a) make firing fallible — a miss chance, a jam that costs a turn, or a retaliation roll on a non-killing shot; keep the flat damage, the point is only that it cannot be a free win. (b) Add a WeaponDef peer to EnemyDef {dmgMin, dmgMax, noise, armorPierce, durabilityCost, retaliateModifier}, resolve melee against the equipped artifact, and drop to a bare-hands profile at durability 0. (c) Add HEAVY ATTACK (double damage, double noise, guaranteed retaliation roll) and PUSH (0 damage, clears alerted, -0.3 on your next slip) — with strike/fire/slip/retreat that is six of the six verbs FR-CBT-02 specifies. The Riot's armor stops being a firearm gate and becomes a weapon-selection problem. Improvised and environmental actions (FR-CBT-03 — lure, trap, chokepoint, the gas leak) stay deferred. Not byte-identical. || [DONE 2026-09-13 - docs/qa/QA_REVIEW_T80.md. Engine 815 -> 846 (+31), harness 264, content-loader 23, testlab 22, schema 160, a11y OK, CI green. Save v10 holds: the one new field, CombatState.offBalance, is OPTIONAL and absent-reads-as-false (the Horde.stepHours shape from T74), so there is no migration rung. Not byte-identical, declared. THE DEFECT, RE-DERIVED BEFORE FIXING (measure/t80.ts on the pre-T80 tree, 3000 duels/cell): firing was a 0.0% chance of a wound and a 0.0% chance of a bite against every enemy that does not burst on death - literally zero, because resolveFire never called enemyRetaliate - against melee's 56.8%/29.1% on a walker and 99.0%/89.2% (4.41 wounds, 9.93h) on a Riot; and melee damage was drawInt(1,2) whatever the player held, so FR-PLR-04 was inverted into 'equipment defines a maintenance cost'. SHIPPED: (a) NEW src/combat/weapons.ts - WeaponDef{dmgMin,dmgMax,noise,armorPierce,durabilityCost,retaliateModifier,accuracy} as the peer of EnemyDef, a 5-row WEAPONS table keyed by ITEM TYPE (weapon.bare, item.tool-reinforced, pistol/shotgun/rifle), weaponFor(state) resolving the equipped artifact with a BROKEN weapon (durability 0) dropping to bare hands, plus effectiveDamage/retaliateChance/surestOf as pure functions. weapon.bare is the pre-T80 melee profile EXACTLY (1-2, noise 15, no pierce/wear/modifier, accuracy 1 = no draw), which is why 814 of the 815 existing tests passed unedited. (b) resolveFire takes an accuracy roll, spends the round + hour + 75 noise whether or not it lands, and calls enemyRetaliate at FIRE_RETALIATE_CHANCE 0.25 on any shot that leaves the body standing. (c) HEAVY (x2 damage, x2 noise, x2 durability, always answered) and PUSH (no damage, no answer, clears alerted and sets offBalance = 45 points off the next escape roll, spent by the next blow, not offered twice) - with strike/fire/slip/retreat that is FR-CBT-02's six, under a mapping written into combatChoices' doc comment: two of the six are existing verbs renamed (aim=fire, hide=slip), so the honest count of what T80 adds is TWO. TWO CORRECTIONS THE MEASUREMENT FORCED: (1) 'guaranteed retaliation' read as 'if it is still standing' made HEAVY STRICTLY DOMINANT - 1.49h/49.4% hurt against strike's 2.25h/56.8% on a walker, and 1.00h/0.0% against a crawler, because double damage kills so often the guarantee never fired. A guarantee you escape by winning is not a cost, so the answer is unconditional, including on the swing that kills. (2) A miss chance and a retaliation term are each INERT alone: swept by rebuild, at accuracy 1.00 the retaliation term leaves the walker column at 0.0%/1.00 rounds - unchanged - because a single round kills it. 0.75 shipped: a body costs a third more ammo (1.00 -> 1.33 rounds) while the walker wound rate stays under 10%. Melee columns IDENTICAL on both trees (the bare-hands claim proved, not asserted). Equipment: the reinforced tool takes a walker from 2.25h/56.8% to 1.49h/19.3% and the Riot from 9.93h/99.0%/4.41 wounds to 2.25h/46.2%/0.50 - armor stops being a firearm gate and becomes a weapon-selection problem. The shove on a loud chasing node (T77: 85% of real escapes) takes the parting-wound rate from 94.7% to 75.0% for one hour and no damage. NOT inert in bot play, unlike T78/T79: the testlab soak goes 1104 actions/70 combats -> 1079/64 with heavy added to FIGHT_KINDS (1144/81 with the bots' old tactics), all 24 runs still passing every invariant. AUDIT: 35 mutants, round 1 26 killed / 9 survived, round 2 35/35 with no survivors; eight of the nine survivors were TEST defects, not code defects. A process failure is recorded in the review: a tool timeout killed a mutation run mid-mutant and the next run scored a meaningless 35/35 against a tree that was still mutated - the runner now refuses to start unless diff -r against a pre-audit snapshot is empty. Also corrected: the design review's claim that no recipe installs room.workshop is OUT OF DATE (recipe.shelter.workshop installs it), so the weapon axis is reachable, just long. New parking lot: PL-M5-36 (shotgun/rifle rows unreachable - pistol is the only firearm in any loot table, so every measured firearm figure is a pistol figure), PL-M5-37 (no gun choice, no pistol-whip), PL-M5-38 (firing is still the SAFEST verb - the dominance is reduced, not removed, and the rest is ammo scarcity = T59), PL-M5-39 (HEAVY's price is wounds, and wounds cannot kill you until PL-M5-01 is settled in T82). PL-M4-30 (molotov has no combat action) REMAINS OPEN - FR-CBT-03 improvised/environmental verbs stay deferred as the task note scoped them. Enemy dials untouched: no EnemyDef value moved, so content/enemies/*.json and its harness drift-guard are unchanged. Next: T81 (seq 104) - melee weapon content, the firefighter's axe, into the socket this task built.]

tasks.title: Melee weapon content — the firefighter's axe
tasks.note: Design review 2026-09-12 (docs/qa/DESIGN_REVIEW_2026_09.md) step 6. FR-CBT-04. Pure content once T80 exists, and it fills the emptiest hole in the build: THERE ARE NO MELEE WEAPONS IN THE GAME. The complete weapon roster referenced anywhere in the engine is item.pistol, item.rifle, item.shotgun and item.molotov (which has no combat action). No bat, no crowbar, no machete, no axe, no knife, no pipe, no brick. The GDD promises five categories with distinct trade-offs — improvised (pipe, brick, chair leg), bladed (knife, machete, axe), blunt (bat, crowbar, hammer), firearms, explosives — and ships two. This matters more than a content gap because you correctly forbade XP and character levels (FR-PLR-10, 'attempts to add one should be rejected'), which makes GEAR THE ONLY PROGRESSION AXIS IN THE GAME, and it is empty. The firefighter's axe is named three times in your own GDD (Principle 6, Part X legendary items, the Manifesto) as the model of what a meaningful level-up looks like, and it cannot currently exist. Ship the categories with real damage/noise/durability/armorPierce profiles against T80's WeaponDef, wire them into the police/industrial/residential loot tables with rarity weighting, and give the best of them the artifact provenance metadata that already exists (PL-M4-33's repair ledger — 'its third repair, it carries the marks now'). Depends on T80. || [DONE 2026-09-13 - docs/qa/QA_REVIEW_T81.md. Engine 846 -> 880 (+34), harness 264 -> 270, content-loader 23, testlab 22, schema gate 160 -> 173 (a FOURTEENTH content type), a11y OK, CI green. Save v10 holds and this task adds NO new state shape: a found weapon is an ItemInstance + an itemId'd InventoryEntry, both of which have existed since T51 - the only change is that something other than the bench now creates one. Not byte-identical for a run that registers the weapon pool; a run without it draws loot bit-for-bit as before, and that is tested. THE BRIEF WAS WRONG ABOUT ONE THING AND THE MEASUREMENT FOUND IT: 'pure content once T80 exists' is false, because player.equipment[WEAPON_SLOT] had EXACTLY ONE WRITER in the whole engine (the crafting bench's mint) and ItemInstance was only ever constructed there - so a weapon placed in a loot table would have arrived as a stack with no durability, no ledger and NO WAY INTO A HAND. Measured pre-T81 (measure/t81.ts, 30 scavenging runs on the shipped city): 0/30 runs ever held a melee weapon, 0/316 combat turns fought armed, 0 melee weapons in any loot table, content/weapons/ an empty directory since M0, and item.pistol coming out of 24.6% of police searches - a gun exactly as likely as a bandage. SHIPPED: (a) EIGHT new melee rows across the GDD Part IX families - improvised (chair leg, pipe), bladed (kitchen knife, machete, the FIREFIGHTER'S AXE), blunt (claw hammer, baseball bat, crowbar) - plus four new WeaponDef fields (category, startDurability, lootWeight, lootKinds); the anti-power-tier rule is ENFORCED by a test that walks every melee row against every other on seven axes (damage/noise/wear/retaliation/pierce/durability/carry weight) and fails on any strictly-dominated row: none. (b) content/weapons/*.json + weapon.schema.json, a fourteenth schema-gated content type, with a harness DRIFT GUARD asserting engine and content agree 1:1 with no orphan either way (the ENEMIES pattern). (c) RegionGraph.weapons as the placement gate (T50/T51/T52 discipline) - no pool, no weapons, exact pre-T81 uniform draw. (d) drawWeighted, the rarity primitive drawPick could not express, costing exactly ONE drawInt step so the stream advances identically. (e) pocketWeapon: a found weapon becomes a tracked artifact with {foundDay, foundAt, repairs: []}, taken up on the spot ONLY when that is not a decision (empty or broken hands); the full-pack rule and its no-debit half are preserved. (f) a new actions/gear.ts EQUIP verb (free, explore-branch only - you cannot swap weapons mid-fight), and dropArtifact, without which every junk weapon a run found was WELDED INTO THE PACK for the rest of it. (g) artifactMarks: provenance in words, never numbers - 'mended once' / 'it carries the marks now' (SCR-10's own sentence, at the third repair) / 'about to go' / 'broken' - closing the rendering half of PL-M4-33, surfaced at the point of decision ('Strike with the baseball bat (worn)'). ONE T80 LABEL REBASELINED deliberately: T80 let the suffix vanish when a weapon broke, which was fine for a bench tool with fifty swings; a chair leg has six, so a broken weapon is now NAMED. MEASURED before -> after: runs that ever held a melee weapon 0/30 (0%) -> 34/60 (57%), first weapon on day 1.26 after 3.9 searches; combat turns fought ARMED 0/316 (0.0%) -> 123/528 (23.3%); P(melee weapon per search) 0.0% -> residential 12.8 / store 10.2 / generic 9.7 / police 9.1 / industrial 8.9 / medical 0.0; item.pistol 24.6% -> 4.7%; the firefighter's axe found by 32.0% of runs that search every police node in the city clean (impossible before). Duel table, walker E[h]/P(hurt)/P(bite): bare 2.26/56.2/30.4, chair leg 2.25/56.7/30.6, knife 1.77/41.7/21.5, machete 1.33/15.6/8.0, AXE 1.00/0.0/0.0; Riot: bare 10.09/99.1/88.8 -> axe 1.66/23.0/11.1. THREE DIALS THE MEASUREMENT FORCED: (1) BASE_LOOT_WEIGHT swept by rebuild 12/18/24/36 -> 68/57/45/37% of runs armed; 18 is the SMALLEST value at which a majority of short runs ever hold something, and run length is FLAT across the whole sweep so the dial is pure frequency. (2) The axe's lootWeight swept 1/2/3/4 -> 12.5/22.0/30.5/41.0% of full police sweeps; 1 left the legendary at one run in eight (decoration wearing a legendary's name) and 4 made it as likely as a pistol. (3) A PROBE DEFECT, recorded because it produced a clean false trend: the first scavenging bot preferred the free equip verb above everything, ping-ponged between two carried weapons and burned its action budget, so the sweep reported 'more weapons => shorter runs' (3.78d at base 12 vs 4.48d at 36) - entirely the instrument. Removing equip from its preference list flattened it to 4.63-4.68d. AND THE SURPRISE (PL-M5-40, NOT dialled away): damage buys noise PER BLOW but the reverse PER KILL, because noise is deposited per swing and a harder hitter needs fewer - the axe banks 30.0 points putting a walker down against bare hands' 33.9, and 49.7 against 151.3 on a Riot. Arming yourself makes the city QUIETER; the axe's real price is rarity, carry weight 8 (a fifth of the pack) and 33 swings before it needs a bench. AUDIT: 42 mutants, round 1 39/42, round 2 (survivors) 3/3, round 3 (full set, current tree) 42/42 with the tree verified pristine before and after. ALL THREE SURVIVORS WERE TEST DEFECTS: every find test called resolveSearchLoot DIRECTLY, so none could see whether the pipeline ever passed weaponsActive(graph) at all (the dead-wiring class this task exists to close - fixed with an end-to-end played-search test); the pool-less test emptied the pack between searches to keep the probe alive and then asserted on the FINAL inventory, throwing away the evidence; and no test found two weapons of the same type before the clock moved, so the artifact-id collision backstop was never exercised. CLOSES PL-M5-36 (all three firearms now placed) and the rendering half of PL-M4-33. DECLARED LIMITS: four of the GDD's five families ship - explosives are still unbuilt (item.molotov has no combat action, PL-M4-30); placement is per node KIND not per node, so the axe comes out of any police node rather than the fire station whose description names the tool wall (PL-M5-41, T84's richness work); PL-M5-37 goes LIVE rather than closing - firearmFor now brings up the surer AND louder shotgun over the pistol with no way to ask for the quiet one; essentially INERT in the testlab soak (1079 actions/64 combats -> 1077/62, mean end day 4.3 either side) exactly as T78/T79 were, because the Lab's policies do not prioritise searching; the equip verb is free, out-of-combat only and has no unequip (PL-M5-42); and wounds still cannot kill you (PL-M5-01), so a better weapon buys hours and infection risk rather than survival.]

tasks.title: Combat stakes — grabbed, companions in the fight, Last Stand trigger
tasks.note: Design review 2026-09-12 (docs/qa/DESIGN_REVIEW_2026_09.md) step 11. CLOSES PL-M4-07; supplies the trigger T62 authors the scene for. Two holes. (1) COMPANIONS DO NOT EXIST IN COMBAT — combat.ts contains zero references to them (the module header admits it: 'combat participation and full autonomy, FR-NPC-03 remainder'). A companion standing beside you contributes no damage, soaks nothing, distracts nothing, and cannot be bitten. killCompanion() is exported from index.ts:588 and is called by NOTHING, so the 'permanent, remembered death' the module sells can only be triggered by deliberately starving someone. With no risk term anywhere, recruiting is unambiguously always correct and PARTY_CAP 3 is a ceiling rather than a decision. Fix: each companion at the node on order:follow contributes an attack roll off its own named stream and is a valid target (a wound to c.condition.wounds, an infection roll on a bite); gate participation on trust >= ORDER_TRUST_MIN so low-trust companions hang back, which gives the trust ladder teeth beyond an order menu; wire killCompanion to the fatal branch. (2) A fight has no shape and no lose state — the player has no health at all (CharacterState is needs/wounds/infection/mind; the only hp in the codebase is the enemy's), so a fight is a wound-severity slot machine you always walk away from. Add a GRABBED outcome as a third result on the retaliation roll: while grabbed, retreat is not offered and strikes deal less, and breaking free costs a turn — that creates the opening/committed/escape arc the GDD's 'desperation' category describes. Then trigger the Last Stand on woundBurden >= threshold AND combat !== null AND no discovered escape target. NOTE: whether the player should have health at all is the one open design question from the review — 'injuries are stories, not -10 HP' taken to its limit is defensible, but it is nowhere written down as a decision, it contradicts the GDD's own core-stats list, and it is what makes the Last Stand structurally impossible rather than merely unbuilt. Settle it before building this. Depends on T80. || [DONE 2026-09-13 - docs/qa/QA_REVIEW_T82.md. Engine 880 -> 911 (+31), harness 270, content-loader 23, testlab 22, schema 173, a11y OK, CI green. SETTLES PL-M5-01 AS ADR-0007 (design/decisions/0007-player-health.md): the player has NO health stat and will not get one - woundBurden IS the health model, never shown as a number, and the GDD Part V 'Health - 0 = death' line is SUPERSEDED by Principle 2. Death in combat is a SITUATION, not a threshold. Save v10 holds: the one new field, CombatState.grabbed, is OPTIONAL and absent-reads-as-false (the offBalance shape from T80), and the Last Stand stores nothing at all - runEndReason stays DERIVED. Not byte-identical, declared. MEASURED BEFORE BUILDING (measure/t82.ts, committed): combat.ts contained ZERO references to companions; killCompanion had ZERO call sites in the whole engine despite being exported since T36; and a bare-handed player beat a RIOT 100.0% of the time at 99.5% wounded / 88.8% bitten. The party probe pairs every row ON THE SAME SEED, so 'party 0' and 'party 3' came out BYTE-IDENTICAL to the digit - three companions changed nothing at all. THE BRIEF'S TRIGGER WAS UNBUILDABLE AS WRITTEN and the measurement found it: the third conjunct, 'no discovered escape target', is not reachable - escapeTargets falls back to every DISCOVERED neighbour (T77's FR-CBT-05 fallback) and relocatePlayer discovers a node's neighbours on arrival, so 0 of 380 combat turns across 2716 turns ever had fewer than TWO. Built as briefed the Last Stand would have been code that could never execute - the T81 'no path to the player' defect in a new place. That is WHY grabbed and the Last Stand are one task: the grab is what makes 'out of options' reachable. SHIPPED: (a) GRABBED - CombatState.grabbed, a third outcome on a retaliation that was ALREADY LANDING, costing NO new combat draw (it is the bottom GRAB_CHANCE 1/3 of the interval the float was already compared against - the T81 drawWeighted trick). While held, every retreat is withheld, push is withheld, your MELEE drops to bare hands whatever you carry, and a new verb 'break' (Tear yourself loose) is the only way out. (b) THE PARTY IN THE FIGHT - fightingCompanions(): alive, here, standing order FOLLOW, trust >= ORDER_TRUST_MIN 80. Each swings 1-2 at 40% off a NEW 'party' RNG stream (so a solo run never touches it), each adds COMPANION_SOAK 0.2 to the chance a blow lands on them instead of you, capped at 0.5, and one past COMPANION_FATAL_BURDEN 60 DIES - through killCompanion, which now has its FIRST CALLER IN THE PROJECT'S HISTORY. The trust ladder finally buys something other than a menu entry. (c) THE LAST STAND - LAST_STAND_AT 80; runEndReason returns 'lastStand' FIRST, ahead of infection and thirst, because a player who is held, badly hurt and also out of water died in the grapple. (d) RUN_END_REASONS - a drift guard the task was FORCED to build: testlab/checks.ts held a hand-written copy of the reason list and failed 11 of 24 soak runs on CORRECT behaviour the moment a fourth reason existed; three copies now derive from the engine, behind a Record<RunEndReason,true> that will not compile if a future reason is forgotten. MEASURED AFTER, 120 bot runs a policy: runs ending in a fight - fights-everything 64%, disengages-when-hurt 8%, three-trusted-companions 7%. All three were 0% before. Duel: bare-handed vs a Riot 100.0% win -> 26.0%. DIALS, ALL SWEPT BY REBUILD: LAST_STAND_AT 60/80/120/160 -> 68/64/55/48% brawler and 20/8/3/0% careful (160 makes a careful player ABSOLUTELY IMMUNE, and a canonical death scene nobody can reach is worse than none); COMPANION_FATAL_BURDEN 40/60/70/100 -> 40/5/2/ZERO companions lost of 360 (the first cut, 100, lost NONE - a party you cannot lose makes recruiting free again); COMPANION_SOAK 0.3-uncapped made a party of three a POWER TIER (Riot 100.0% win at 19.5% hurt) so the total is capped at half; BREAK_BASE 0.35/0.45/0.55/0.70. GRAB_CHANCE turns out NOT to be a lethality dial at all - halving it moves the Last Stand share 1-2 points where the threshold moves it 20. THREE DEFECTS THE BUILD INTRODUCED, ALL CAUGHT BEFORE SHIPPING: (1) BREAK FREE WAS A FREE ACTION - the first resolveBreak never called enemyRetaliate, so a break turn wounded the player 0 times in 400 seeded Riot fights where a strike wounded 212. The mechanic designed to corner you shipped with a risk-free exit: T80's dominant-HEAVY defect from the other direction. A failed attempt is now answered, a successful one is not. (2) A DEAD ENEMY KEPT SWINGING - when a COMPANION landed the killing blow the corpse, already cleared from combat and removed from the roster, still took a draw and landed a wound on 15% of party kill turns; the only path by which a bite and its infection clock could come from something already dead. (3) A DEAD AFFORDANCE the TEST SUITE found first: the brief's 'strikes deal less' implemented as a half-damage multiplier lands on 1 every time on the 1-2 bare-hands band, and 1 is exactly the Riot's armor - so a grabbed bare-handed player dealt LITERALLY ZERO damage to a Riot forever while 'strike' sat on the menu costing an hour. Replaced by dropping to the bare-hands PROFILE, which reuses the fallback a broken weapon already takes. NOT INERT IN BOT PLAY, unlike T78/T79/T81: the testlab soak goes {infection 6, dehydrated 18} / 1077 actions / 62 combats -> {lastStand 11, infection 5, dehydrated 8} / 955 actions / 44 combats, mean end day 4.3 -> 3.8. tasks.note: DONE 2026-09-14. Design review 2026-09-12 step 12a. Exploration, node identity and loot as a YIELD. Three of the brief's four claims held; one had already been shipped by T81 and the measurement said so. (1) NodeDef.richness (0-250, default 100) scales the REGION term of the yield cap - trunc(regionLoot*richness/800) - trunc(searchPct/34), which is the pre-T84 formula exactly at 100 - behind an active-system gate (richnessAuthored, the T83 claimable precedent), and all 60 nodes are authored from their own descriptions. Distinct caps per region 1 -> 6-10; the 8 interchangeable industrial nodes of region.ironworks go from 7/7/7/7/7/7/7/7 to 15/13/12/11/10/9/8/4; mean cap across the city 6.62 -> 6.67, so the authoring redistributes rather than buffs. (2) THE SEARCH ROLL WAS A FEE AND IS NOW A HAUL. Measured pre-T84: items per search flat at 1.00 at every cap while the mean take ran 1.00 -> 5.45, so the richer the district the more of the shared stock you burned for the same single item. Same drawInt, same stream, but the number is now the haul: ceil(points/LOOT_POINTS_PER_ITEM) items, one table draw each, and the region debited by what was actually carried. The T18 full-pack rule is preserved exactly, generalized per unit. tasks.title: Base tradeoffs — room slots, a water source, per-unit purification
tasks.note: Design review 2026-09-12 (docs/qa/DESIGN_REVIEW_2026_09.md) step 12b. The base is finished on day three and has no decisions in it. The entire REACHABLE upgrade tree is claim + fortify + rooftop garden + watchtower = 5 scrap, 2 water and 12 hours, roughly five searches' worth of loot; nothing is mutually exclusive, nothing competes for a slot, and NodeState.rooms is an unbounded array. Worse, the tree has an unbuildable half: no recipe installs room.workshop, so the generator recipe's room gate never opens, so room.generator is unreachable, so job.generator and job.salvage are unreachable — only 2 of 6 jobs can ever be unlocked, and item.blueprint.antibiotics drops at 20% in medical nodes and unlocks nothing. Fix: (a) add NodeDef.roomSlots (3-5, varying by building — the marina has fewer than a warehouse) and gate installsRoom on free slots, with demolition recovering half the scrap; instantly garden-or-cistern and workshop-or-medical become real choices and WHICH BUILDING YOU CLAIMED acquires a 20-hour tail. (b) Close the workshop gap so the job tree is completable. (c) Add a water source. Water is the hard bottleneck and its ONLY source is a 14.3% loot draw in 2 of 6 node kinds: the player needs ~0.87/day, a based resident burns ~1.2/day (residents get a worse exchange rate than the player — 40 relief per unit against the player's 55), so ONE companion already exceeds a full day of searching and community growth is arithmetically impossible. Ship the purify recipes capped at their inputs per craft (economy.ts:434-444 currently converts the player's ENTIRE carried dirty-water stack for one set of inputs, so the correct play is always to hoard to the pack limit and purify once) plus a room.cistern + job.water. That single addition gives item.water-dirty and item.charcoal a purpose, gives item.fuel its recurring sink, makes companions affordable so PARTY_CAP 3 becomes a decision, and creates the game's first real X-or-Y: fuel burned on water is fuel not burned on power or molotovs. Also reconcile order:scavenge (1 can/2h, no prerequisite) with the jobs system it strictly dominates, and fix job.kitchen, which converts fresh food (60 relief) into canned (45) to prevent spoilage that cannot happen — refrigerated is always true because powerGrid never falls below POWER_SPOIL_AT 40 (the drain is trunc(powerPressure*h/6), which is 0 on a 2h turn in anything short of a storm). Depends on T74.

tasks.title: The terminal project — a win condition and a run that escalates toward it
tasks.note: Design review 2026-09-12 (docs/qa/DESIGN_REVIEW_2026_09.md) step 10. FR-STY-06 groundwork and the direct fix for 'hour 20 has a NARROWER decision space than hour 2'. runEndReason (survival.ts:261) returns exactly 'starved' | 'dehydrated' | 'infection' — three ways to lose and ZERO ways to win; story.endingFlags is an empty stub; grep the engine for win/victory/extraction/evacuat/escape and there are no hits. GDD XVI's fourth run phase, Legacy ('the run resolves toward its ending: hold, escape, sacrifice, or fall'), has no mechanism, and the original Kik-bot outline this project reimagines specified win conditions the reimagining currently lacks. Meanwhile the long arc is a monotonic decline with no counterplay: loot is finite and only falls (~180-210 items in the entire city, and the contest drains regions on a wall clock whether you visit or not — Rivermouth empties itself by about day 8 even if you never enter it), the base is done on day 3, and nothing renews water. Fix: a 3-4 stage departure-or-holdout project the base builds — a vehicle, a long-range transmitter, a fortified block — whose inputs are deliberately the resources the economy over-produces and never spends. item.batteries, item.lighter, item.blanket and item.charcoal currently have ZERO consumers anywhere in the codebase and item.tools has exactly one, once, ever; this is their sink, with no new items invented. CRITICALLY: each completed stage must RAISE something — noise, region threat, or survivorActivity (the loot-contest driver) — so building toward escape makes the city harder and the last week of a run is a race rather than a wind-down, which is the only shape consistent with 'a slow, uneven decline that the player fights to slow down'. Depends on T85 (the base needs slots and an economy worth spending) and T78 (the escalation must be able to land). Feeds T61 directly — you cannot assemble rescue/entrenchment/sacrifice endings from run components until the run has components other than death.

Radio sonic identity per signal type (AUDIO §6.6, FR-AUD-04, Could/v1): the tuning/static grammar and the four distinct broadcast timbres (emergency loop / military / civilian voice / number station). The radio's non-audio equivalent already ships as the T50 listen digest (renderSignalRead), so the soundscape leaves radio to it; the per-type sonic texture is a later block.

Accessibility audio settings (AUDIO §11): a caption-verbosity / reduce-startle toggle set now, and the eventual per-bus volume sliders, mono downmix, the two mix profiles, and the hearing-damage + infection-distortion reductions, belong with the T56 accessibility settings surface. In a text client the captions are always-on (you can't mute the only channel), so the first-pass need is a verbosity/quiet toggle, not per-bus mixing.

Hearing-damage (tinnitus) as a PLAYED state (AUDIO §6.4): a close gunshot/blast dropping the world into muffle+ring for a stretch, deaf to threat cues, is a MECHANIC (it changes what the player can perceive) and so an engine concern - not this side-effect-free presentation pass. Noted for a later combat-audio task, alongside distinguishing the player's own gunshot as a discrete louder cue (§6.1/§6.3), a fidelity win the current 'it's loud here' line approximates.

Dial calibration: the non-identity difficulty magnitudes (Story/Hardcore/Nightmare) are directional FIRST-PASS; the real numbers come from the M5 staged balance passes (GDD XIX - survivability/scarcity/pacing) against the 'one more day' target. Only the Survivor identity column is permanent.

Dial resolution floor (audit's systemic note): lootContest/lootYield act on base magnitudes often equal to 1, where trunc(1 x m) erases any multiplier in the open interval (1,2) - so at Rivermouth's starting region activity Hardcore/Nightmare loot contest resolves IDENTICALLY to Survivor. M5 must fix this STRUCTURALLY (raise the base granularity or carry the fractional remainder across ticks), not by re-picking magnitudes alone (the same trap that made the pre-audit director dial dead; the director dial is now out of it via integer steps).

Ironman client enforcement: one save slot, autosave-over, no reload, delete-on-death. The engine records meta.ironman and exposes isIronman(state); the actual single-slot / no-take-back enforcement is a client save-slot policy, not the demo CLI's single zurvival-save.json. needDrift scales the PLAYER's survival clock only (ratified scope decision: companions and residents are sustained by the shelter economy, so their scarcity rides the loot/stash dials, not a personal drift multiplier). Extending needDrift to companion/NPC drift so a harder mode's clock reaches everyone is a coherent M5 tuning option.

M5 web/native SCREEN-READER runtime parity (NFR-ACC-02 runtime): aria-live scene announcements, focus-managed drill-down dialogs, choices as a labelled button list. OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, settle before T82: the player has no health stat. CharacterState is {needs, wounds, infection, mind}; the only hp in the codebase belongs to the enemy (CombatState); runEndReason returns starved | dehydrated | infection. A zombie cannot kill you — combat costs resources, time and mobility but never the run. This may be a deliberate and defensible reading of Principle 2 ('damage is never a generic -10 HP'), but it is nowhere recorded as a decision, it contradicts the GDD's own core-stats list ('Health — 0 = death'), and it is what makes the Last Stand structurally impossible rather than merely unbuilt. Log the answer as an ADR either way.

Wound TYPE is mechanically inert. WOUND_EFFECTS declares 'bleed' | 'slow' | 'weaken' | 'infect-risk' and the only read anywhere is === 'infect-risk', so a sprain, a fracture and a laceration are identical to each other and to a paper cut: WOUND_FATIGUE_PER_WOUND 1 per hour. Three if-branches would make wound type matter for the first time — 'slow' adds hours to MOVE_COST, 'weaken' caps MELEE_DMG_MAX at 1, 'bleed' adds to detectChance and drives the scent trail (FR-INJ-03, Principle 2's flagship example, which is quoted in the README and the GDD three times and does not exist in the engine). Also: burn, concussion and illness are 3 of the GDD's 6 named wounds and are unshipped — concussion in particular would pair with the perception-distortion tech infection already built.

The infection cure race is arithmetically unwinnable by its own advertised verbs, and the real escape is unsignposted. At terminal, cure E[removed] is 0.4*18 + 0.6*4 = 9.6 per 4h dose while the driver adds 8 in those same 4 hours — net E[-1.6]. The actual escape is closing the bite wound with plain `treat`, because advanceInfection returns early when the wound is shut and nothing ever decays progression afterwards. That is a genuinely elegant lesson ('stop the driver, don't fight the fever') and the infection menu never points at it. SIGNPOST it — do not retune the dials. Related: infectionSign ('the sheen of fever on you') is defined and no NPC system reads it, so nobody reacts to a visibly infected player.

Radio signals pay in prose, not world state. SignalDef carries label + messages{live,failing,dead} and nothing else — there is no revealsNode, no marksDiscovery, no grantsLead, no flag — so the derived-status model (which is genuinely good craft: append-only latches, status computed from powerGrid and regional threat, never stored) is an atmosphere channel that can never tell a player something they can act on. NpcLead already proves the pattern with `reveals` and `marks`; give SignalDef the same two fields plus setsFlag and resolve them in listen() when effectiveStatus is live. Also BROADCAST_OUTCOMES is 3 hardcoded strings drawn uniformly and outcome 3 ('you hear the dead turn, and start to come') spawns nothing — the noise deposit is identical across all three, so the outcome text is decorative.

NodeState.damage, corpses, blood, traps, occupants and playerNotes are seeded and never written (T84 takes corpses/blood). player.economy.freshness is one clock for the whole carried stack and nulls out at zero units, so dropping your last fresh item resets the 48h timer for free.

A job that is already stalled when a tick BEGINS (full grid, full wall, missing input) banks no hours for that tick, even if the stall clears inside it. With the shipped garden->kitchen pairing on an empty stash, 24 hours played as 1h/2h/4h turns all yield 1 fresh + 3 canned, while a single 24-hour advanceWorld yields 4 fresh + 0 canned, because the kitchen had nothing to cook at the instant the advance began. The PLAYED path is the accurate one, so this costs the player nothing today (advanceWorld has no production caller) - but it is the third of T74's lossy-by-design rules and the only one that is a scheduling artifact rather than a deliberate choice. Fixing it means interleaving job cycles within a tick in time order, which is a scheduler, not an accumulator.

Two house-wide clock idioms T75's audit surfaced, both T66 material. The player therefore has no lever that permanently reduces horde pressure, only ones that route it. T83 material, alongside the night-attack half of the same system.

On the shipped city EVERY director escalate beat is a day-1 beat: 24 of 24 under both runner policies and 4 of 4 in the 20-day idle probe, none after day 1 in 889 measured turns. The low band (DIRECTOR_LOW_BAND 25) is reached only while globalThreat climbs from 0 on the first day; anchored pressure then sits at 34-50. After day 1 the director is a relief/hold device, and for an UNDISTRESSED player it is idle (director ON vs OFF identical on the idle probe, 63/63). The T30 DoD holds under distress (ON 55.9 vs OFF 62.6 end density). Whether a district pacified 15+ points below its anchor would re-open the beat is unmeasured (nothing in play lowers a region dial except relief itself). Options for T60: retune the band, or make the bands RELATIVE to the region's anchor so 'calm' means 'calmer than authored'.

The neglect differential is barely readable in the shipped UI. harness/src/screens.ts#threatWord is the only place a district's threat reaches the player (quiet/uneasy/dangerous/deadly on the travel list), so a 10-point gap between a patrolled district and an abandoned one shows up as a different WORD on only 8 of 40 days (d13-d20 on both seeds, 'uneasy' vs 'dangerous') before the day ramp carries the patrolled one over the same threshold. Nothing anywhere says how long it has been since the player was in a district or which way it is moving. Candidates: a days-since-visit line on the travel list, a trend arrow on the region readout, or an authored beat that fires on re-entering a district that has festered since you left (nothing but drift currently reads the neglect term at all).

The 100 ceiling absorbs the neglect term on exactly the two districts the design most wants dangerous. The day ramp alone carries Mercy's anchor (authored 80) to the clamp on day 21 and Downtown's (70) on day 31, so from there neglect adds nothing and the T78/T79 trees read identical dials for them at d40 (100/100 and 99/98). It does register before that (Downtown 83/92 -> 93/99 at day 14), so the term expires on them rather than being lost. The binding constraint is the dial's headroom, not the term: either the top districts need room above their authored point (a soft cap, or authored baselines that leave headroom for the ramp+neglect+bias stack), or the escalation needs to express itself in something other than a 0-100 dial once a district is at capacity. Pairs with PL-M5-11 (difficulty spread at d30 is zero bodies) and PL-M5-12 (riot/bloated dormant at carrying capacity).

[CLOSED 2026-09-13 by T81] Two of the three firearm rows in WEAPONS are unreachable content on the shipped city. item.pistol is the only firearm in any loot table (sim/loot.ts, the police table), encounter or start kit, so item.shotgun (accuracy 0.85, noise 85, retaliate -10) and item.rifle (0.80, 95, +10) can only be held by a hand-built state. Every firearm figure quoted in QA_REVIEW_T80 is therefore a PISTOL figure, and the accuracy/noise/handling triangle the table describes is authored rather than played. T81 places weapons into loot; it should either place these two or the rows should be cut rather than left as decoration. RESOLUTION: T81 placed all three firearms in the police table at their own rarity weights (pistol 3, shotgun 1, rifle 1 against BASE_LOOT_WEIGHT 18) and shotgun additionally in residential; measured at 4.7% / 1.5% / 1.3% of police searches. No firearm figure is a pistol figure by default any more. NB this makes PL-M5-37 LIVE rather than hypothetical: a player can now genuinely carry two guns and firearmFor brings up the surer AND louder one.

[NOW LIVE 2026-09-13 - T81 closed PL-M5-36] The player cannot choose which firearm fires and cannot pistol-whip. firearmFor() brings up the SUREST gun in the pack (ties by id), so a player carrying both a pistol and a rifle can never choose the quieter one - a real tactical choice (noise 75 vs 95) that the menu does not offer, deliberately, because a three-gun menu for a game that can only hand you one gun would be three-quarters decoration. Separately, an equipped firearm reads as bare hands for the melee question: there is no pistol-whip verb. Revisit once PL-M5-36 makes a second firearm reachable.

Firing is still the safest verb against every enemy in the game - the design review's dominant strategy is REDUCED, not removed. Measured post-T80: a walker costs 1.33 rounds and carries a 7.8% chance of a wound against melee's 56.8%; a Riot 2.67 rounds and 38.5% against 99.0%. That gap is correct in kind (a gun should be the safe answer) and its remaining size is a question about how scarce ammo and how loud noise actually are in play, which is the balance pass's question, not this task's. T59 should re-run measure/t80.ts against whatever ammo economy it settles on rather than re-deriving the fight arithmetic.

HEAVY's entire price is a guaranteed wound, and wounds cannot kill the player (PL-M5-01 - CharacterState has no health and runEndReason is starved/dehydrated/infection). So the committed swing currently trades hours for infection risk and wound burden rather than for danger, and its cost is carried by systems T82 may reshape when it settles whether the player should have health at all. If T82 adds a health term or the GRABBED outcome, re-measure the heavy/strike trade against it (measure/t80.ts --weapon) before assuming the dial still reads the same.

Noise is deposited PER SWING, so a harder hitter is quieter PER KILL - the opposite of what the roster's 'damage buys noise' authoring implies. Measured over 3000 duels a cell: putting a walker down with the firefighter's axe (noise 30, one blow) banks 30.0 noise points against bare hands' 33.9 (noise 15, E[2.26] blows), and on a Riot it is 49.7 against 151.3. So arming yourself makes the city QUIETER, and the loudest-swing counterweight the axe is authored with does not actually price its power. T81 declined to dial this away: if noise is meant to price power, the deposit has to scale with the damage DEALT rather than with the swing, which changes every weapon's relationship to T75/T76's noise chain at once. T59/T60 should settle it before quoting any per-kill noise figure.

[NARROWED by T84 2026-09-14] Richness makes node.the-terraces.fire-station (170) the BEST place to look for the axe rather than the only one, but placement is still per node KIND, so city hall and the evac checkpoint still yield it. Node-specific placement is still unbuilt and still a real axis. Original: Weapon placement is per node KIND, not per node. WeaponDef.lootKinds names 'police', so the firefighter's axe comes out of city hall, the evac checkpoint and the police post exactly as readily as out of node.the-terraces.fire-station - whose own authored description names the tool wall it should come off ('axes, halligans, bolt cutters'). The legendary's home is therefore generic. Node-specific placement belongs with T84's NodeDef.richness work, which is already adding the per-node loot axis; do it there rather than bolting a node list onto WeaponDef.

The equip verb (actions/gear.ts) is free (EQUIP_COST 0, the T18 pack-management rule), offered in the quiet explore branch ONLY - so there is no mid-fight weapon swap, which is deliberate (a free in-fight swap would collapse the carry-weight trade the roster is balanced on) - and there is no unequip verb: dropping the artifact is how you empty a hand. Carrying three weapons and switching between fights therefore costs nothing but weight, and indecision costs nothing at all. Separately, nothing PROMPTS before the swing that breaks a weapon: the label reads 'about to go' below 25 durability, which is a warning the player must read rather than a decision the game puts in front of them. Revisit alongside T82's combat stakes.

The GDD Part IX names five weapon families and the build now ships four. T80 shipped firearms; T81 shipped improvised, bladed and blunt. EXPLOSIVES remain unbuilt: item.molotov is craftable (recipe.weapon.molotov) and carryable and has no combat action at all, which is PL-M4-30 still open since M4 Part 7. A thrown-weapon / area-fire verb is the missing piece, and it is also the natural home for FR-CBT-03's improvised and environmental actions (lure, trap, chokepoint, the gas leak), which T80 deferred and T81 did not touch.

The Last Stand is an ENDING, not yet a STAND. runEndReason is evaluated before any choice is offered, so the blow that completes the condition (in a fight, grabbed, woundBurden >= LAST_STAND_AT) ends the run on the SAME FRAME - the player gets no final turn, no last set of choices, and nothing to spend, which is precisely what GDD IX asks a Last Stand to be ('a final, heightened sequence where the player spends whatever they have left'). treat is not offered inside a fight either, so no bandage can be reached once the condition is met; the bandage's job is to stop you ever meeting it. T82 delivers the TRIGGER plus one line of placeholder prose. T62 authors the scene, and endingNarration('lastStand') is the only branch in that function expected to be replaced rather than kept.

LAST_STAND_AT is a flat 80 on every difficulty mode - Story and Ironman alike - and was never run through sim/difficulty.ts's scalar dials. Almost certainly wrong at both ends: Story's whole premise is a gentler run, and Ironman's is a harsher one. T59/T60's to settle with the rest of the balance pass, alongside PL-M5-27's parting-wound table.

T82's grab prices MELEE and leaves FIREARMS completely untouched: resolveFire does not consult weaponInFight, and a shot fired point-blank at something holding you is exactly as accurate and as damaging as any other shot (combatChoices still offers it, relabelled 'Fire point blank'). So an armed player's only cost for the grab is the lost retreat, which WIDENS PL-M5-38 ('firing is still the safest verb against everything') rather than narrowing it. The fix belongs with T59/T60's balance pass or with the explosives verb, not smuggled into a combat-stakes task.

A wounded companion can NEVER be treated. tickCompanions drifts their needs and nothing heals their wounds; the T35 share verbs pass food and water, not bandages; and advanceInfection is called only for the player (sim/survival.ts), so a companion's bite is inert over time rather than a clock. A fighting companion's wounds therefore accumulate monotonically for the whole run and the player's only lever is the order:hold that keeps them out of the next fight. Measured at T82: 76 open wounds across 345 surviving companions over 120 runs. Pairs with PL-M3-02/05 (off-screen upkeep) and T53.

FORTIFICATION IS ECONOMICALLY OUT OF REACH, so T83's bare-wall row is the row the player actually lives in. Measured over 60 bot runs: peak scrap carried averages 0.3-0.4 units across a WHOLE RUN, `fortify` is chosen 0.1 times per claimed run, and a claimed base carries any wall at all on 4.2% of based turns (109 of 2579). One scrap buys FORTIFY_GAIN 25 points and FORTIFY_DECAY_PER_HOUR erases them in a day. The T83 --wall table shows 25 points of wall removes the breach entirely, so the siege HAS an answer; the player just cannot afford it. T85's economy brief is where that becomes payable - this is measured here and deliberately not patched here.

T83's narrowed sanctuary locks the player out of the remedy at the moment of collision. availableActions returns overrunChoices before it ever reaches shelterChoices, so at a 0-wall base with a mass standing on it the player is offered flight and the hold and can neither `fortify` nor `abandon-shelter`. Fortifying answers the siege BEFORE the night, never during it. Either overrunChoices should admit the at-your-own-base verbs, or the docs should stop implying fortify is available when it matters.

THE TESTLAB SOAK NEVER EXERCISES THE SHELTER AT ALL. Measured directly on both trees: the testlab's four policies (random/careful/greedy/fighter) claim a base in 0 of 32 runs. Five tasks of shelter work - T37 claim, T38 fortify, T39 stash, T52 jobs, T83 siege - are invisible to the project's own soak, which is why T83 re-baselines to 2519 -> 2517 actions with an identical end mix. A `homesteader` policy that settles, fortifies and sleeps would make the soak cover the half of the game it currently cannot see.

Two of the base's three immunities survive T83. repopulate.ts still hard-excludes shelterId from spawning and hordes.ts#massAction still refuses to shed a body there, neither of them reading `barricades`. So a mass standing ON the base is counted by siegePressure at hop 0 while leaving nothing behind it, and a breached base (shelterId null) immediately becomes eligible for both - a discontinuity nobody has looked at. T84/T85 territory.

T83's tickSiege resolves every banked night against ONE FROZEN SNAPSHOT of hordes/noise/density, because the world layers run before it in both the pipeline and advanceWorld. So a played night and a fast-forwarded one produce the same COUNT of sieges but not the same outcomes - disproved on 2 of 5 seeds through advanceWorld (0 sieges vs 1, base kept vs base lost). Same declared class as sim/clocks.ts's RNG-per-tick exception and T76's horde body trade. Interleaving a world tick between banked nights would close it.

The player is 10% of the loot economy. Measured over 40 bot runs: a run consumes 228 of the city 395 loot points, of which the player searches account for 23.3 (10.2%) and the OFF-SCREEN CONTEST for 204.7 (89.8%). So "the search roll taxes a finite, SHARED stock" is true and economically trivial - the shared half is a wall clock the player cannot influence, and halving or doubling what a search takes moves a tenth of the drain. Whether that split is right is a scarcity-balance question (T59/T60); recorded here because T84 measured it and deliberately did not change it.

A run still touches three nodes. Post-T84: 3.15 distinct nodes searched per run, 2.85 of 6 kinds seen, 7-11 of 60 nodes discovered, mean end day 3.9. Sixty nodes of hand-authored richness are read by a run that visits five percent of them, and the map-as-journal pillar assumes a player who returns to places. Per-node identity is now IN the build; whether a player lives long enough to learn the city is a run-length question and run length is T59/T60.

Nothing narrates a search haul. SearchHaul carries found/offered/taken/packFull and applyPlayerAction takes .state and drops the rest, so a player learns what a search returned by reading their pack - and with hauls now up to six items and partial refusals routine, that is less feedback than the single-item build gave. The one consequence T84 did owe them ships (a "barely any room left" clause in sceneOf, live at PACK_HEAVY). A per-search find list is a narration/client task, not a simulation one.

The leave-behind question is pressure, not yet a choice. Turns at or over PACK_HEAVY went 0.7% -> 14.3% and pack peak 19.04 -> 22.57 of 40, but the same 40 runs record 0.0 full-pack turns and 0.00 drops taken. The pack is now something a run notices; it is not yet something a run has to answer. LOOT_POINTS_PER_ITEM 2 reaches 29.1% and a full pack in one run in ten - the dial is live and the conservative end was chosen deliberately, so this is T59/T60 to close, not a defect.
